bounded_statement: Each first-collection source unit ea01–ea12, which the task states is identified by k1 and measured by column a, appears on exactly two staged rows, and the workflow feeds all 24 resulting a-values into scipy's independent-samples t-test, a procedure that treats every entry as an independent observation; the report's df=46 confirms all repeated unit entries were counted as independent, so the same authorized unit was repeatedly entered into a row-independent procedure.

counterevidence_considered.description: The task instructs applying the procedure to the complete staged row sequence, which could be read as authorizing entry of every row as-is; however, this authorizes the rows as input, not treating repeated measurements of one declared unit as independent observations.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: instruction to use complete row sequence

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

counterevidence_considered.description: The k2 codes (eb01–eb24) are all distinct, so the second collection's entries are not repeated; the issue is demonstrated only on the k1 side.

evidence.observed_value: k1 = source-unit identifier for column a

evidence.description: The same k1 unit appears on multiple rows: ea01 occurs on two consecutive rows with two different a-values, and this two-rows-per-unit pattern runs through ea12.
evidence.observed_value: 12 distinct ea units across 24 rows, each contributing 2 a-values

evidence.description: All row-level a-values are fed unaggregated into an independent-samples t-test, which assumes each entry is an independent observation.
evidence.observed_value: st.ttest_ind over 24 left entries from 12 units

source_refs.quoted_text:
left = [float(row["a"]) for row in staged]
right = [float(row["b"]) for row in staged]
result = st.ttest_ind(left, right)

evidence.description: The selected report shows df=46 (24+24-2), confirming the duplicated unit entries were counted as independent observations in the produced result.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify by (1) checking whether equal ea codes could denote different units — the task states k1 identifies a source item and provides no basis for splitting equal codes into distinct units; (2) checking whether the procedure accounts for repetition — st.ttest_ind has no grouping mechanism and the reported df=46 proves all 24 entries per side were treated as independent; and (3) checking whether the disclaimer that row pairing is a storage convention removes the problem — it addresses cross-column pairing, not within-column repetition of the same unit. All falsification routes failed, so the demonstrated verdict stands.

root_cause: The workflow passes every row's a-value directly into st.ttest_ind without aggregating or deduplicating by the k1 unit identifier, so the two measurements per ea-unit are counted as two independent observations, inflating the effective sample size of the first collection from 12 units to 24 entries.
